subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should bundled Slack support user-level Events API routing and no-APP-badge replies as a regular Slack user identity, and what explicit opt-in authorization/audit boundary is required?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but enabling OpenClaw to receive and speak as a human Slack account changes identity, authorization, and audit expectations beyond a routine channel bug fix.

options.title: Design explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Add a named opt-in Slack mode with authorization matching, send-token selection, docs, tests, and live Slack proof before enabling user-level event handling.

options.title: Document bot-only Slack ingress
options.body: Keep bundled Slack scoped to bot/app identity and document that DMs must target the Slack app or bot rather than a regular user account.

options.title: Prototype outside core first
options.body: Ask for an external plugin or fork proof of the user-token event and reply model before deciding whether to promote it into bundled Slack.

recommendation.title: Design explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Add a named opt-in Slack mode with authorization matching, send-token selection, docs, tests, and live Slack proof before enabling user-level event handling.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent Slack identity, token, docs, and current-file history makes steipete the best available routing owner for the security-boundary choice.
